📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leading thanks to Stephen Humphrys’ early goal, City failed to add to their tally by the interval against a rock-bottom Reds side who were very unconvincing at the back, especially in the first half.

A spirited start to the second period from a Reds side without a win in their previous 10 league games created a sense of unease at Valley Parade.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

But a second goal midway through the second half from ex-Barnsley forward Humphrys settled the contest. Substitute Jake Beesley added a stoppage-time penalty.

Duff said: “I was disappointed at half-time because I thought we should have been put the game to bed.

"I didn't think we started the game particularly well, but Humps demonstrated a little bit of quality that he’s got.

It has been revealed that "We lost too many duels in the first half. We just felt that once we won a duel and made a couple of passes, we got in.

"If I was playing centre-half in the team, I’d have picked one of the forwards up and throttled him at half-time.

"You live on a knife-edge constantly, and the longer it goes on, you feel the nerves in the stadium.

"We weren't particularly good today, but I don't think we're in a position where we can start turning our nose up with 3-0 wins at home.

In a recent development, "We were better on Saturday and drew. The positive is it’s the first time we’ve scored three goals in 51 league games and it’s one defeat in 17 now.

In a recent development, "We need to be more clinical. You're not always going to create that many chances in the game.

According to recent reports, "The forwards know that. Like I said, it's not a nice feeling living on a knife-edge, living on a bounce of a ball or an overhead kick, like we were on Saturday.

"We have to put the game to bed and I think once the second goal went in, it calmed a little bit.

"Barnsley are random in the way that they play. They put people in strange positions and it's really difficult to play against.

It has been revealed that "But when you do turn it over, they're wide open. So, I just felt that's where those duels were important.

"I know people will say they're bottom of the league but it's not easy winning a game of football. We've seen that.

"I watched them play Sheffield Wednesday last Friday, and after the first 10 minutes, they dominated the game.

"We have to be respectful of what we're up against and be humble enough to go, ‘we can improve’.

The Saints comfortably outplayed the Blades in the first half-hour and deservedly took the lead through Lewis Dobbin. But from there, the hosts took the initiative and made far better use of the ball than Southampton did, even if it took until the 90th minute for Sydie Peck to find the equaliser.

But Wilder was proud of his team's efforts against a Championship side he greatly respects.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It has been revealed that "I was proud of the players today for the way they really stood up to the challenge," he commented. "I thought when the bullets were flying, they were there.

"They took the ball in the second half.

"They took the ball in the first half, they just gave the ball away too cheaply in the first 20, 25 minutes.

"If you allow really good players the opportunity to get on the ball they'll dictate the game, which they did.

Sources indicate that "But I was absolutely delighted with it. I'm proud of the players, the way they got themselves back in the game.

"Tactically, we got ourselves back in the game and sorted that situation out and really drove and dominated, and everybody stepped into the game.".

Michael Cooper made a crucial save from substitute Samuel Edozie in stoppage time to preserve the point, and Wilder felt it was no less than his side deserved.

"I think it would have been the cruellest of cruel blows if they'd have nicked a winner, and I think we definitely deserve something from the game, with the attitude, the way we played, and how brave we were," remarked Wilder.

"It was a difficult (first) 25 minutes for the players to deal with, but I wanted them to show courage, and they all did, they all stepped up to it, and we had the performance second half that was worthy of a result against the top side.

"I don't think anybody's done that to them all season, I don't think anybody's done that since Tonda (Eckert) took over.

"Getting back on the coach, they might say they had an opportunity to win it, which they did, when the left-back just appeared from nowhere, coming off the pitch and we get caught up in the game.

"You're all caught up in the emotion of the game, and it was an emotional game.

"I want us to play with that emotion, and 100 per cent as soon as the ball went in the back of the net, with Sydie's finish it was, we want to go for a win.

"When the boy counter-attacks off the left, and he finds Finn Azaz, who's a top player, and he finds a pass, you're thinking really, 'Come on, we deserve a little bit better than that.'.

"But Michael pulled off a top save.

"Sometimes, when you look back on draws, it's bigger than just the draw, with the performance against a side of the quality that we played against.".

Xabi Alonso has been warned that Joao Pedro’s return from injury may not be the silver bullet needed to resurrect Chelsea’s form.

The Spaniard’s side have won just one of their last five matches in all competitions, slumping to a 4-1 home collapse against Leeds United last time out.

Injuries have hamstrung the Blues, with captain Reece James and £115m man Moises Caicedo among those sharing the treatment room with Pedro, but Alonso’s issues cut deeper.

Chelsea’s alarming dip in form appeared to coincide with the absences of Joao Pedro, but former Chelsea star Joe Cole said that the Brazilian’s return will not outweigh the Blues’ calamitous defending.

He said: “The team is not playing well, with Joao Pedro coming back in will help, but the whole of the set-up at Chelsea needs to be better.

“The players need to step up and perform, and they need to stop conceding goals. I think that's the crucial thing with Chelsea, they need to stop conceding goals.”.

The Brazilian striker has scored 20 Premier League goals since joining the club last season, but a thigh injury sustained in training last month has left him sidelined, and he is not expected to return until the new year.

In a record worse than all but four top-flight sides, the Blues’ backline has shipped 20 goals so far this term, almost double the tally conceded at this stage of last season.

Cole, who lifted three league titles with Chelsea during a seven-year stint in West London, also weighed in on rumours linking Bournemouth’s Alex Scott to a sensational move.

Standard Sport reported last month that Scott is available for sale for an offer in excess of £100m, with Alonso’s Chelsea weighing up a January move.

Cole, appearing on the Dressing Room podcast sponsored by BOYLE Sports, said: “Alex Scott is a great player, he's going to be linked. Chelsea are linked with players like that at the moment, we're buying players from Bournemouth rather than taking players from around Real Madrid or Barcelona.

Several AC Milan players have been highly praised by the Italian media after the 5-1 dismantling of Frosinone at San Siro.

Milan ended up with goals from five different sources as Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted, in addition to the opening goal which was an own-goal by Calvani. Adrien Rabiot got three assists, while Diego Moreira shone too.

It was a statement result and a ruthless display of the weapons that the Rossoneri have in transition, and it moves Ruben Amorim’s side back into the top four, while they remain five points off leaders Lazio.

Starting with La Gazzetta dello Sport, they gave the team’s overall performance a score of 8 out of 10, which is the same mark that they gave Amorim for his selections and tactical handling of what could have been a tough game on paper.

Recent findings suggest that rabiot was the Serie A Man of the Match and he gets the crown from La Gazzetta too, scoring an 8. The worst performer was Davide Bartesaghi, who struggled in his battle with Ghedjemis and got a 5.5.

In a recent development, moreira matched Rabiot with an 8, while Pulisic and Luka Modric were given a 7.5. Four players scored a 7: Yunus Musah, Ramos, Jashari and Cisse. Sankhoun Diawara (6.5) passed the test, with Koni De Winter, Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan being given a 6.

Sources indicate that corriere dello Sport were a tad harsher with their scoring, giving Rabiot a 7.5 as the highest score. Jashari, Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and Ramos were handed a 7. They gave Cisse a 6.5, and everyone else got a passing score. Amorim (7.5) was also praised.

Tuttosport meanwhile gave Rabiot an 8, distributing 7.5s instead to Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and the coach Amorim. Scores of 7 went to Jashari, Musah, Ramos and Cisse. Gila, De Winter and Diawara got given a 6.5, and everyone else a 6.

Gary Neville was left ‘absolutely stunned’ by Mauricio Pochettino’s decision to recall Matthijs de Ligt after the defender’s blunder allowed Liverpool to make their breakthrough in a rampant 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

A seemingly innocuous hoiked pass over the top from Liverpool full-back Ronald Araujo wreaked havoc inside United’s half in the tenth minute, leading to Dominik Szoboszlai’s superb opener.

De Ligt had been thrown in for his first appearance of the Premier League season and there were obvious signs of rustiness early on as the Dutchman bizarrely let Araujo’s hopeful ball run through to Alexander Isak.

Isak’s eyes will have lit up as he raced in behind in acres of space and United were guilty of yet more calamitous defending just moments later as Leny Yoro clattered into the back of the Liverpool striker on the edge of the penalty area.

Referee Samuel Barrott wasted little time in showing Yoro a straight red card for the clumsy foul, reducing the visitors to ten men in a nightmare start to Pochettino’s reign as manager.

United’s woes were soon compounded as Szoboszlai struck the resulting free-kick emphatically beyond a despairing Senne Lammes to break the deadlock and send the Anfield crowd into raptures.

Liverpool were not done there, though, and it was Florian Wirtz who directed home Rio Ngumoha’s cross with an audacious flicked finish to double the hosts’ advantage inside only 13 minutes.

A pair of well-taken goals from Ngumoha and Victor Munoz further increased the deficit in a dominant second half for Andoni Iraola’s men, who finished the weekend three points clear of Bournemouth in fourth place.

When watching back replays of the catalogue of errors leading to Liverpool’s opener, former United full-back Neville revealed just how ‘stunned’ he had been left by the decision to select De Ligt in the first place.

‘When I saw Matthijs de Ligt’s name on the teamsheet, I have to be honest with you, I was absolutely stunned,’ Neville said on Sky Sports’ commentary of the match.

Industry observers note that ‘That is just a basic ball over the top of him. It’s his problem to start with.’.

Though De Ligt was the main focus of Neville’s criticism, Yoro did not escape without receiving some barbs of his own.

‘Leny Yoro can be further across but if you look at De Ligt in this channel, he’s miles away from him,’ Neville added.

Industry observers note that ‘Yoro should be across, yes, he can get further around. He has to cover and he doesn’t. He reacts late, his anticipation is really poor.

‘And because he doesn’t play the ball, Yoro, it could be outside the box but it is a red card.

‘It’s so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these kinds of mistakes.’.

According to Neville, Yoro had displayed great ‘naivety’ in getting himself sent off so early in the Premier League contest.

‘He’s not happy with it, Mauricio Pochettino,’ the ex-England international continued.

‘You could argue with it, Isak just delays slightly to make sure that Yoro runs into the back of him.

‘But unfortunately, when you’re a young defender, you’re going to get caught like that and it’s naivety.’.

Switching his focus back to De Ligt, Neville noted the Netherlands international had likely been ‘exposed’ as a result of playing so little football over the last 12 months.

Industry observers note that ‘We saw it against Como and he’s been out for a year, trying to come back to this level of football. It’s really tough,’ he went on.

‘To have De Ligt out there in a game like this, in a back four, he’s been exposed inside the first ten minutes.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I have to say, Yoro’s positioning covering is really poor. It’s poor.

‘Yoro has got to be across and around the other centre-back. You’ve got to cover your mate and he doesn’t. It’s really just bad all round from Manchester United.

‘Michael Carrick will be watching this at home and thinking, “Yeah, that’s what I was having to deal with two weeks ago”, it’s so poor.’.

Neville’s Sky Sports’ colleague Jamie Carragher was similarly unimpressed by United’s defending, branding the visitors’ start ‘absolutely shocking’.

‘It’s as bad as it gets from two centre-backs,’ the former Liverpool and England defender mentioned.

‘The ball from Ronald Araujo… it wasn’t even a pass, it’s just a clearance, a hopeful ball through the middle.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction.
  • Sources indicate that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk.
  • But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Sources indicate that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

It has been revealed that for Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Recent findings suggest that keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews mentioned. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

Industry observers note that brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

It has been revealed that to play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak stated. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very crucial points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola stated they will now be out “for some time”.

The loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

Industry observers note that the injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their significant-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa said: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.

A 2-1 triumph over Motherwell on Saturday night stretched Rangers' unbeaten run to 13 matches after Ryan Naderi struck a late winner at Fir Park.

McInnes' side will host a revitalised Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night, before two further home matches against Falkirk and Dundee United over the next week.

They will then face a double-header against Hibs, with a league clash at Easter Road swiftly followed by the cup final.

McInnes insists no player is guaranteed their place in the team - and challenged them to earn their place for the Hampden showpiece as they look to win the first trophy of the season.

'I think the squad looks strong at the minute,' noted the Ibrox boss. 'We've got good options and good options from the bench to turn to.

Derek McInnes has led Rangers on a 13-game unbeaten run in all competitions.

'In this little run of fixtures, hopefully everybody will start to play a wee bit more of their part and hopefully more winning performances.

'I don't think I'll mention it [the cup final] too often, but they are not daft, they see that and everybody wants to play in the team.

'Anybody who's in the team needs to keep playing well to stay in the team and anybody who's not in the team needs to train right and take advantage of their minutes.

'We make that point often enough. Sometimes you've got to go away to tough venues like Motherwell and do the hard work and get the reward.

'But there's bigger games, more games like cup finals to take part in, so everybody wants to play in that one.

'I'm sure it does us no harm. I think it keeps the fans bubbling along, a chance of silverware, so when it comes along hopefully, as I say, we're in good form.'.

Rangers are on a strong run of form and haven't lost a game since they were dumped out of Europe against Jablonec at the end of August.

The victory over Motherwell maintained their position in second in the table, four points adrift of Celtic with a game in hand.

Up against an Aberdeen side buoyed by their first win under upcoming boss Mario Frick at the weekend, McInnes wants his players to keep the pedal to the metal.

'I think it's unusual with five games now away from Ibrox, four in the league and the cup game, and now the fixtures kind of run the other way,' stated the Rangers boss.

'We've got some good fixtures at home but I think we always look at little blocks in the weeks, and where we're looking to try and get to by a certain period, and get certain points and certain targets.

'But first thing's first now with Aberdeen. We've got to make sure we're a strong home team again. Hopefully we can score a few more goals but, ultimately, as long as we win the game, I'll be happy.

'I think there's always a wee concern when you've got so many away on an international break, but obviously now with the January break gone, this is us working right through to March.

'When you look at those little blocks of games, and where the teams are, it's vital that we just put our shoulder to the wheel.

Sources indicate that 'Every game is going to bring up different challenges and just because we're at Ibrox, it's an advantage, but it doesn't guarantee anything. We've got to use that advantage properly.

Recent findings suggest that 'As I say, we've got some fixtures now ahead of the cup final. Hopefully we can get into the cup final in good form and with some strong performances.'.

Venezuelan striker Kevin Kelsy could be in line to start against Aberdeen.

Kevin Kelsy could be in line for a bigger role this week after fatigue caused by his return from international duty limited his involvement in Saturday's win over Motherwell.

The Venezuela striker was only fit enough for a substitute appearance after enduring a gruelling journey back from a friendly in Russia, with Derek McInnes admitting the travel disruption had taken its toll.

'When you go away on international duty, they go to some far-flung places and playing a friendly in Russia is not the best preparation,' said the Rangers boss.

Sources indicate that 'There was a point on Thursday morning when we were really worried about whether he was getting back. To have ten-and-a-half hours in an airport all day Thursday isn't ideal preparation.

Industry observers note that 'He was gubbed on Friday. He was very tired when he spoke to me and told me he hadn't really slept.

Industry observers note that 'It's been a bit unusual, the preparation. We sent him home early on Friday to get a good sleep and look after himself, but we just made the call we thought was the right thing to do.

'We needed everybody at it on Saturday and we've got a significant week ahead of us where he can play his part, hopefully from the start in one or two of these games.'.

Mauricio Pochettino remarked Manchester United were on the wrong end of an ‘unfair’ decision during their heavy Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Pochettino’s reign as United manager began in dismal fashion at Anfield as his side were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.

The defining moment of the match came after just eight minutes as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

Isak’s touch was heavy and United goalkeeper Senne Lammens quickly retrieved the ball but referee Samuel Barrott still deemed a red card to be the suitable punishment.

To make matters worse for Manchester United, Dominik Szoboszlai blasted home the subsequent free-kick to put the hosts ahead.

Liverpool scored again just five minutes later – Florian Wirtz volleying home a cross from the lively Rio Ngumoha.

England winger Ngumoha, 18, scored Liverpool’s third 20 minutes into the second half before Víctor Munoz added a fourth late on.

Pochettino described his first match as Manchester United manager as ‘painful and disappointing’ but criticised the early red card that paved the way for the heavy defeat.

Sources indicate that ‘So painful. So disappointed,’ Pochettino said in his post-match interview. ‘It’s not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it’s so painful.

‘The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to the calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality.

Sources indicate that leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

‘We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field. We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.’.

In a recent development, pochettino, who was hired as Michael Carrick’s replacement last week, added: ‘The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

‘When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper; he runs and goes down.

In a recent development, ‘In Leny’s case, it wasn’t intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.

‘If you look before, on the sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo. Similar? No. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty.

According to recent reports, ‘How that changes life, if you score after six minutes. Now, for sure, we are talking in a different way. We have to take responsibility; I take the responsibility. We keep pushing.

‘It’s not going to change what happened. Being respectful is the most important. At the same time, I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel.

‘That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card.’.

Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone prior to the November international break, when Carrick was relieved of his duties.

Results over the weekend leave the Red Devils second from bottom in the Premier League with just eight points from their first 11 games of the campaign.

Liverpool, meanwhile, climb back into the Champions League places after an emphatic win over United.

Anfield boss Andoni Iraola mentioned: ‘We have been very good away this season but at home we haven’t been good enough and still haven’t been good enough.

‘We needed a major game, and Manchester United is always a big game, to finish like this.

‘It’s true the game’s condition changes because they play with 10 most of the game, but still we’ve done our job, we controlled the game and I think it’s always nice when you can win like this in these kind of games.’.

Asked for his take on the early red card, Iraola added: ‘I think he’s the last man, no? It’s a clear foul and a red card, yes?’.

Manchester United and Liverpool both return to Champions League action this week, with the former travelling to Sporting and the latter visiting Club Brugge.

Andoni Iraola was keen to play down Liverpool’s Premier League title hoeps in the wake of his side’s 4-0 win over Manchester United.

The rampant Reds ensured it was a miserable day for new Red Devils boss Mauricio Pochettino, who saw his side 2-0 down and reduced to 10 men after just 13 minute.

In truth, the margin of victory could have been much greater were it not for some wasteful finishing, but second half strikes from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz put the gloss on an emphatic victory.

With Arsenal having dropped points at Newcastle on Saturday, Liverpool have reduced the gap at the top to seven points and recovered some ground following their defeat to the champions at Anfield nearly a month ago.

Asked, after the first landmark victory of his tenure, whether Liverpool were in the title race, however, Pochettino was keen to play down expectations.

‘It’s still early days,’ Iraola told Sky Sports. ‘I think we are missing the two significant games we lost here at home between Arsenal and [Manchester City] they are making the difference in the standings.

According to recent reports, ‘This is still so early. This doesn’t stop because we have a very difficult game against Borussia Dortmund and then we have the big derby.’.

There was no getting away, though, from the chasm that exists between the two north west heavyweights and Iraola was thrilled with what his burgeoning team delivered in front of their own fans.

Florian Wirtz and Ngumoha were particularly to the fore and the Spaniard was keen to praise two key members of his attacking cohort.

‘I think Rio if you can put him in situations where they can’t help the full-back, he is very difficult to stop especially inside the box,’ he said of the England international. ‘He can go both ways.’.

On the apparently rejuvenated Wirtz, he added: ‘He’s in a lovely moment and we want to keep him there as much as we can.

‘He’s in a situation against 10 players where you need players like him to control the situation and see the passes in behind.

‘He’s also arriving more and not just scoring but being a threat. He’s becoming another option and I’m happy with him.’.

Tottenham have been linked to Piero Ausilio, with the former Inter Milan sporting director earmarked for a similar role at the Premier League club.

Italian outlet Tuttosport report that Spurs are closing in on a deal to bring Ausilio to north London.

It is hoped that Ausilio could be installed in time to take charge of Spurs’ transfer approach for the January transfer window.

Tottenham’s executive structure has frequently changed since 2023.

Fabio Paratici joined the club in 2021 as sporting director, but stepped down in April 2023 ahead of a 30-month ban from all football activities handed to him by FIFA after a conviction for financial malpractice.

Paratici returned to his role in October 2025 after the conclusion of his suspension, sharing duties with co-sporting director Johan Lange.

But his return did not last long, as Paratici quit Spurs in February of this year, meaning Lange stepped up to become sole sporting director.

Ausilio ended a 28-year association with Inter Milan in the summer, with the Italian giants deciding not to renew his contract as sporting director.

Initially joining the club’s youth academy in 1998, Ausilio worked his way through the ranks to become sporting director in 2014.

Industry observers note that midway through his first season in his role, Ausilio was named as the TMW award’s best sporting director at the start of 2015. In 2024 Ausilio was recognised as the ‘best sporting director’ in football at the Globe Soccer Awards.

Retiring from football after injury as a teenager, Ausilio holds a degree in law, having studied at the University of Milan.

Over the years Ausilio has garnered a strong reputation for his scouting and squad-building, helping to construct a team at the San Siro that has won three Serie A titles and reached the Champions League final twice in the past five seasons.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Florian Wirtz was quick to shut down any suggestion that Liverpool were spending too much time ‘thinking about’ Arsenal after their 4-0 win over Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start in what was ultimately a mismatch between the two bitter rivals, with the Red Devils proving their own worst enemy and giving themselves a mountain to climb early on at Anfield.

Some calamitous defending from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s tenth-minute breakthrough and saw the latter shown a straight red card by referee Samuel Barrott, a decision that only compounded the visitors’ woes.

The impressive Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s advantage with an audacious finish just three minutes later to send the home crowd into raptures, before a pair of second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz completed the rout.

Having cut a frustrated figure on the touchline for the most part, Pochettino made it clear he was less than impressed by the officiating on show as he faced the media shortly after the final whistle on Merseyside.

The Argentinian will no doubt be desperate to turn the tide when United return to Premier League action at home to Brentford in six days’ time, following a midweek trip to Sporting.

The result ensured Pochettino’s men finished the weekend just one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace, with the Old Trafford giants now leading Europe’s top five leagues for most goals conceded (34 in all competitions).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Liverpool, meanwhile, moved four points clear of fifth-placed Bournemouth and just one point behind Arsenal’s two nearest rivals, Manchester City and Brighton, after ten games.

‘Really good. The atmosphere after the game was so good. We could enjoy it and it was just a nice afternoon,’ Wirtz – named man of the match – said of the victory in his post-match interview with Sky Sports.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I feel very good but it’s also because the team develops and gets better.

‘Just being part of this, you also get better, so I’m just enjoying that.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Asked if he was perhaps benefitting from being coached by Andoni Iraola and Jurgen Klopp at club and international level, Wirtz replied: ‘Both are very good coaches and I enjoy playing under both.

‘They both bring different qualities and I’m just happy and can be happy to have two of these coaches.’.

Victory in next Sunday’s Merseyside derby at Everton would see Liverpool move to within four points of Arsenal, who host Manchester City later that same afternoon.

When asked if the 4-0 thumping of United had taken Liverpool to ‘another level’, Wirtz replied: ‘Yeah, it was definitely vital today, also for the table situation.

‘I think a lot of teams on top of the table, they didn’t win this weekend so it’s good that we could use the chance.

‘The red card influenced the game a bit of course but we take that, we earned it because of the run of Alex [Isak] so yeah, very good.’.

Wirtz was then asked if he was ‘thinking about’ Arsenal and possibility of winning the league this season, and his answer was unequivocal.

It came after the Gunners – the reigning Premier League champions – surrendered a first-half lead to drop points away to Newcastle.

‘Uh, I wasn’t talking about Arsenal… all the teams, I don’t know, from one to three,’ Wirtz responded.

‘So we knew, we didn’t speak so much about it, but I think everybody knew it was a significant chance to make some points.

‘I’m happy we used this chance.’.

Keane Lewis-Potter netted a quickfire brace to put the Bees in control, before their position was strengthened further by James Tarkowski's 40th-minute red card for a challenge that was deemed dangerous after a VAR review.

In the second half, Vitaly Janelt produced a stunning long-range effort, and Fabio Carvalho netted his second league goal of the season to seal back-to-back home wins.

Lewis-Potter's deflected opener will go down in history as Brentford's 300th Premier League goal.

The milestone strike took place over five years after Sergio Canos scored Brentford's first Premier League goal in a 2-0 victory over Arsenal.

Yoane Wissa may have damaged his relationship with Brentford supporters with the manner of his exit to Newcastle United in the summer of 2025, but he played a key role in the Bees hitting the 300-goal mark, considering he is the club's leading Premier League goalscorer with 45 goals in 137 games.

Bryan Mbeumo is in second place on Brentford's all-time Premier League goalscorer list with 42 strikes in 136 matches.

Ivan Toney, meanwhile, scored 36 goals in 83 top-flight appearances for the Bees before he left for Al-Ahli in 2024.

Two current Brentford stars, Igor Thiago and Kevin Shade, will be looking to chase the tallies of the aforementioned trio, having scored 24 Premier League goals apiece in their time with the West London club.

Brentford will now turn their focus to three high-profile games against Manchester United, Arsenal and Manchester City.

They will travel to Old Trafford this Saturday with hopes of claiming their first-ever Premier League win over Man United, who are reeling from Sunday's heavy 4-0 loss to Liverpool.

Jamie Carragher indicates he ‘felt sorry’ for Matthijs de Ligt during Manchester United’s Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Ten-man United were thumped 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Old Trafford manager.

The visitors were reduced to ten men inside ten minutes as Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

If that early blow was not bad enough, Liverpool took the lead from the subsequent free-kick as Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home yet another set-piece goal.

England international Ngumoha, 18, turned provider to goalscorer in the second-half before Victor Munoz added Liverpool’s fourth late on.

Carragher was particularly critical of De Ligt after the match but remarked he ‘felt sorry’ for the Manchester United centre-back who made his first start of the season at Anfield.

‘I thought it was a really strange decision,’ Carragher noted on Sky Sports when asked about Pochettino’s decision to start De Ligt. ‘It was such a bizarre decision.

‘Not because of his quality because I think he’s a better centre-back than Harry Maguire when you look at what he’s achieved in his career and the clubs he’s played for.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But he hasn’t played football so to play him at Anfield away, it felt so wrong. He was all over the place.

‘He’s played for some top football clubs – Bayern Munich, Ajax and Juventus – those are some of the biggest clubs in the world.

‘So to watch him perform like that… I felt sorry for him.’.

Yet another deflating result leaves Manchester United 19th in the Premier League with just eight points from 11 games.

In a recent development, when that fact was put to Bruno Fernandes, the United captain said: ‘It’s very painful and it hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation.

Guimaraes continued, revealing that when he first arrived in north London, Rice urged him to be patient as he attempted to learn Arteta’s tactical style.

“It’s very complicated to explain to you because it took me ages to understand what he wants.

Industry observers note that “But I think I’m getting there, and I remember when I came, Declan Rice mentioned to me, ‘Bruno, be patient, because it took me like six months to understand exactly what he wants. So be patient, don’t push too much’.

Second-placed Brighton suffered a shock 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull City while Manchester City’s surprising slump continued as Enzo Maresca’s side could only draw 1-1 at home to Fulham.

The only team in the top-four to win this weekend was Liverpool, who smashed ten-man Manchester United 4-0, but the Reds are still a healthy seven points adrift of Arsenal.

Mikel Arteta ended Arsenal’s 22-year wait for a Premier League trophy last season and eight-time title winner Neville expects the Gunners to retain that crown in a ‘very strange’ domestic campaign.

‘Looking at the Premier League top-six right now, Arsenal are clearly the standout team and are going to win the league at a canter,’ Neville noted on his Sky Sports podcast.

Recent findings suggest that ‘But the rest of the usual top five or six teams, it’s not been this bad has it for a long time? They’re really struggling.

According to recent reports, ‘Liverpool were obviously a bit better today but Chelsea are struggling, Tottenham are struggling. Manchester United are struggling, Manchester City look like they’ve fallen off a cliff right now compared to the standards they set under Pep Guardiola.

While Liverpool climbed back into the top-four by beating Manchester United, the Red Devils sunk to 19th in the Premier League.

United were thrashed in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge after Leny Yoro was sent off inside ten minutes at Anfield.

Despite Manchester United’s dismal position, Neville refused to say his former club were in a relegation battle.

Sandro Tonali has returned to training as Tottenham prepare to visit Sunderland this weekend.

The Italian joined Spurs from Newcastle in the summer and has been a mainstay under Roberto De Zerbi, appearing in ten league matches so far.

The £100m man was a surprise absentee from the team-sheet for Saturday’s 2-0 defeat of Ipswich, though, with De Zerbi confirming ahead of kick-off that he had returned from international duty ill.

“(The reasons for the changes to the lineup are) a combination of physical condition (and defeat to Leeds),” he explained.

“Many players, they came back (from international duty) not in the right condition. (Sandro) Tonali was sick for a couple of days. Rodrigo Bentancur arrived yesterday, just yesterday working with us.”.

It was not clear how long Tonali might spend on the sidelines, but it appears he will be available for the trip to Wearside after he was spotted taking part in an open training session on Tuesday.

He appeared to be the only returnee, though, with Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mathys Tel all absent. James Maddison was away from the main group doing indoor work.

Savio returned from a hamstring injury to feature as a substitute against Ipswich, but lasted just 20 minutes before pulling up having re-aggravated the same injury.

According to recent reports, “It is the same injury. And it is the worst thing from today,” said De Zerbi.

Luca Williams-Barnett stole the show on Saturday, bagging a goal and an assist on his full Premier League debut, and continued to train as normal with the first-team.

It has been widely reported he will be handed an improved contract as a reward for breaking into the first team, with confirmation of that news expected in the coming days.

Peter Schmeichel believes simply avoiding relegation should be Mauricio Pochettino’s main ‘target’ at Manchester United this season.

Pochettino took charge of United for the first time away to bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon and it proved a nightmare start for the Argentine, with his side thumped 4-0 at Anfield.

The Red Devils were reduced to ten men in only the tenth minute after Leny Yoro brought down Alexander Isak, and the visitors’ woes were compounded as Dominik Szoboszlai scored with the resulting free-kick.

Man-of-the-match Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s advantage with an audacious finish just three minutes later, before a pair of second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz put the hosts out of sight.

The result ensured United remained firmly in the relegation zone at the end of the weekend’s drama, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

The Old Trafford giants, who now lead Europe’s top five leagues for most goals conceded (34 in all competitions), will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters at Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Realistically, can Manchester United just finish tenth or 12th? It would be okay,’ former United goalkeeper Schmeichel noted on Viaplay following the side’s heavy defeat on Merseyside.

‘I know it’s silly to say but we are in the relegation zone and this team looks like a team that could get relegated.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘So now that should be the target. Weirdly enough, at the moment it looks like it [that avoiding relegation is the target].

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

‘But we [Viaplay’s punditry panel] have all played in the Premier League so we know we’re in November, we’re approaching December, it’s not really now.

‘It’s when we get to March and if they keep doing this for so long, I mean there’s going to be trouble.

‘But I think, at least I have faith that he [Pochettino] can correct those things.

‘He’s never going to make them a championship winning team, not these guys.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It was some calamitous defending from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro that led to Liverpool’s breakthrough against United, with the latter guilty of fouling Alexander Isak after failing to cover his centre-back partner.

And while it was De Ligt that made the initial mistake, Yoro was the main focus of Schmeichel’s post-match criticism.

‘I think Isak is doing really well,’ the Dane mentioned when watching back replays of the move.

‘When Yoro comes in, Isak cuts across him and yes, he brings him down.

‘It’s terrible defending, it is. Not for that on its own but why is he not reading the ball over the top, over De Ligt?

‘Yoro should have been supporting his co-defender and he’s not.’.

Schmeichel has long been an outspoken critic of Lisandro Martinez and branded the defender ‘disgraceful’ in the wake of United’s 2-0 loss to Chelsea last month.

It came just a fortnight after Martinez had launched an explosive attack on United’s board, in which he suggested the squad had been repeatedly let down by the club’s recruitment team.

‘I’m fed up talking about him. Honestly, I’m fed up talking about him,’ Schmeichel mentioned of Martinez following United’s latest setback.

‘He’s a guy that criticises people upstairs, criticises his team-mates… I think you have to perform better than that, I really do think that.

‘You can through not all of the goals, but you can go through a couple of the goals and he’s there, at the centre of that, and he could have done something to at least make it harder for Liverpool to score.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan produced their best attacking display of the season on Sunday night as they put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro.

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani early on set the tone, with Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netting in the rout. The ruthless counter-attacking display moves Milan back inside the top four, after wins from Como, Roma and Lazio earlier in the round.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The match stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals – so scoring double what they created – but also having five major chances which matches the number of goals scored.

Frosinone remarkably had more shots in total (15 to 12), but they were more wasteful with only three on target to the Rossoneri’s eight. The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season.

📊 The stats from the win against Frosinone. pic.twitter.com/ERVTj98m9Y.

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 22, 2026.

Only Nereo Rocco’s (29) and Lajos Czeizler’s (31) Milan sides scored more goals than Ruben Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 matches in charge in Serie A.

Adrien Rabiot is the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal (including goals and assists) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004, and he became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A with more than 10 goals in his first 10 games in a single season.

With his sixth goal in his 10th Serie A appearance for Milan at 20 years and 31 days, Alphadjo Cisse became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato , who achieved it at 18 years and 189 days.

No team has scored more goals than Milan in the first 15 minutes of play in the five major European leagues at the moment underway (7, like Barcelona and Chelsea).

Milan are now unbeaten in all seven meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W5 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

Milan have won five of their last six league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in a run of Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino may have left Gary Neville ‘absolutely stunned’ by picking Matthijs de Ligt against Liverpool, but the Manchester United manager claims there was a simple reason for it.

The new Red Devils boss had a tough opening game in charge as he took his side to Anfield and it ended up being a nightmare debut for the Argentine.

Leny Yoro was shown a red card after eight minutes and Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick.

Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz also netted to complete a comfortable 4-0 win for Andoni Iraola’s men.

Sources indicate that manchester United have now picked up just eight points from 11 games and sit 19th in the Premier League table. Every other club in the division has more wins than the one they have managed.

While the Red Devils clearly have many problems, De Ligt has been a focus of criticism after his performance at Anfield.

The Dutch defender has recovered from a long-term injury, but was starting in the Premier League for the first time in nearly a year, having made two Champions League appearances this season.

The 27-year-old looked a long way off Premier League pace as he was run ragged by the Liverpool front line.

Asked why he went for De Ligt alongside Yoro over Harry Maguire, who started on the bench but has been playing regularly this season, Pochettino mentioned: ‘He was training, he played in Champions League before the international duty. I think, when we arrived we saw the combination.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

He then promptly turned his attention to claiming Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet could have given away a penalty for a challenge on Bryan Mbeumo before Yoro was dismissed.

‘I repeat again, if Jacquet was penalty and the referee say that it’s a penalty, for sure that action after never comes and maybe we’re talking another way,’ he said. ‘But one centre-back made a mistake, wasn’t punished. Us, we made one mistake and we were punished.

‘And now I accept all the situation, but the circumstances were the circumstances and it’s so key to put the circumstances in front, always.’.

Gary Neville watched De Ligt play in the defeat to Como in October and was surprised that he was given the nod at Anfield after his performance in Italy.

‘When I saw Matthijs de Ligt’s name on the teamsheet, I have to be honest with you, I was absolutely stunned,’ Neville mentioned on Sky Sports.

‘The reason I was stunned was because of this: if you watched him against Como four weeks ago, he was very much well off it.’.

Neville added: ‘We saw it against Como and he’s been out for a year, trying to come back to this level of football. It’s really tough.

‘To have De Ligt out there in a game like this, in a back four, he’s been exposed inside the first ten minutes.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 03:08.

Liverpool will travel to take on Belgian title-holders Club Brugge for a Champions League's league-phase clash at Jan Breydel Stadium on Wednesday, hoping to solidify their place in the top eight.

Andoni Iraola's side hammered old enemies Manchester United 4-0 on Sunday, and man of the match Florian Wirtz will be keen to build on his display in midweek.

Alisson Becker should continue in goal amidst reports of new contract negotiations, shielded by a centre-back pairing of Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet, who could be given more rest in the coming weeks with Giovanni Leoni returning to parts of team training this month.

Jeremie Frimpong was brought on as a substitute against United at the weekend, and could start at right-back on Wednesday, while Kostas Tsimikas comes in for Milos Kerkez at left-back.

Youngster Trey Nyoni has become a key part of Iraola's squad of late, and he is likely to line up alongside Alexis Mac Allister in the centre of the park, given that Ryan Gravenberch is a doubt due to a heel fracture and Dominik Szoboszlai recently recovered from a minor hamstring problem.

With Wirtz operating in the number 10 role, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola are the names in the frame out wide, with the latter hoping to find the back of the net after missing a number of chances against the Red Devils.

Cody Gakpo is a doubt after picking up a calf injury on international duty with the Netherlands, while 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha could begin the game on the bench for load management reasons, following his record-breaking goal and assist against Man United.

Alexander Isak has been in exceptional form this season, but he could be rotated in Brugge, leaving space for Lewis Koumas to lead the line on Wednesday.

Liverpool possible starting lineup:.

Alisson; Frimpong, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Nyoni, Mac Allister; Munoz, Wirtz, Barcola; Koumas.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women’s Super League strugglers Crystal Palace have been handed a three-point deduction after breaching substitution rules against Everton in September.
  • Palace opened their WSL campaign with a 1-0 victory over the Toffees thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith’s first-half goal.
  • But they will not be able to keep hold of their points haul from that victory, having made use of a fourth substitution window in second-half injury time, when only three are permitted per match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women’s Super League strugglers Crystal Palace have been handed a three-point deduction after breaching substitution rules against Everton in September.

Palace opened their WSL campaign with a 1-0 victory over the Toffees thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith’s first-half goal.

But they will not be able to keep hold of their points haul from that victory, having made use of a fourth substitution window in second-half injury time, when only three are permitted per match.

That saw them introduce Kirsty Howat in place of Shannon O’Brien in the seventh of eight added minutes.

Industry observers note that A statement from the WSL confirms Crystal Palace admitted their breach of competition rules, while an independent tribunal dubbed the move “inadvertent” and “not intended to secure an unfair advantage”. It also acknowledged Palace have taken steps to ensure the incident would not be repeated.

However, it maintained a sporting sanction would be necessary, writing: “The integrity of the competition would be damaged if a club that had breached the rules on substitution opportunities, and had won the match, were allowed to keep the points it obtained.”.

Howat did not touch the ball in her time on the pitch, which lasted less than one minute, though Everton maintained her introduction handed the Eagles an unfair advantage. The tribunal concurred, adding in their decision that Howat’s lack of influence on the match did not amount to “exceptional circumstances.”.

The imposed three-point deduction will leave Palace on six points with 11 matches played and drop them to 11th place in the table, above only winless Charlton Athletic. Should they finish the season in that position, they would face a play-off with the WSL2’s second-place finisher for their place in the top flight.

Palace said in a club statement that they are “disappointed” by the tribunal’s decision, adding they feel they have been stripped of a “deserved victory.”.

The statement read: “Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty – a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.”.

Palace do not have the option to appeal the tribunal’s decision.

People entering old age now have better memory than their parents did

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Improvements in education, lifestyle and health during early life are slowing rates of cognitive decline in older people.Credit: Laura Olivas/Getty.
  • According to recent reports, people born later in the twentieth century have a better memory when they enter old age and experience slower cognitive decline than do those born earlier, according to a study1 published in Nature Medicine on 17 November.
  • Industry observers note that the researchers analysed data from memory tests that required participants to recall lists of words.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Improvements in education, lifestyle and health during early life are slowing rates of cognitive decline in older people.Credit: Laura Olivas/Getty.

According to recent reports, people born later in the twentieth century have a better memory when they enter old age and experience slower cognitive decline than do those born earlier, according to a study1 published in Nature Medicine on 17 November. The analysis offers clues about why dementia rates have fallen by 13% per decade over the past 27 years in Europe and the United States2.

Industry observers note that the researchers analysed data from memory tests that required participants to recall lists of words. The study included 219,000 people aged 50 and older who were born between 1910 and 1964, and tracked changes in their scores over three decades. These list-based tests are commonly used to screen for dementia and Alzheimer’s disease.

Consistent with previous studies3, people born more recently entered old age with better memory performance compared with those born in earlier generations. A ten-year jump in birth date was associated with a 10% higher memory score at the age of 60. Memory decline also seems to have become less steep across successive generations, says study co-author Anders Fjell, a neuropsychologist at the University of Oslo in Norway.

According to recent reports, the findings are “confirmatory” of other studies on the topic, which indicated that the rate of memory decline is slowing down but weren’t statistically significant, says Carol Brayne, an epidemiologist who studies dementia at the University of Cambridge, UK. “It is another piece of the jigsaw.”.

Recent findings suggest that because many populations around the world are ageing — that is, older individuals are becoming a larger proportion of the total population — the number of people living with dementia is increasing worldwide. But an individual person’s risk of dementia at any given age has dropped by two-thirds over the past 40 years in the United States4. “For those who reach 80, a smaller percentage [of people] will get dementia than before,” explains Fjell.

Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active.

Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active.

Sources indicate that to understand what might be driving this trend, Fjell and his colleagues used longitudinal data on individuals’ cognitive performance to estimate their memory trajectories over time. The authors examined whether people born later in the twentieth century showed differences in their memory performance and their rate of memory decline compared with those born earlier.

The analysis found that with each successive birth decade, people were 64% more likely to maintain stable memory function — that is, experience little or no memory deterioration.

Recent findings suggest that the authors also investigated brain imaging data from nearly 2,000 people over a median of four years. They found that a stable memory during ageing also corresponded to a decrease in shrinkage of the hippocampus — a brain region involved in memory formation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.

Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.

A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, indicated the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.

Recent findings suggest that ‘To all the idiots on my Snapchat, that is a solar eclipse! In France, all they got was a little croissant from the bakery,’ Pepe joked at the time.

Unsurprisingly, the wild rumour quickly spread online amongst fans, many of whom mocked Pepe for apparently going against the advice of experts and wilfully exposing himself to intense visible light, ultraviolet and infrared radiation.

But on Sunday evening, Pepe’s club Villarreal released a statement vehemently denying these baseless claims on social media.

‘Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to observing the solar eclipse,’ the statement from the La Liga outfit read.

Villarreal confirmed that Pepe had indeed undergone surgery but stressed that it was ‘entirely unrelated’ to the solar eclipse.

‘The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event,’ the statement continued.

‘The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health.’.

The surgery Pepe underwent meant the ex-Arsenal attacker was sidelined for Villarreal’s games against Real Madrid, Napoli, Elche, Liverpool and Valencia last month.

The Ivory Coast international made his return in Villarreal’s Copa del Rey first-round tie with Manacor, in which he scored his side’s final goal in a thumping 5-0 victory.

He has gone on to feature in all of Villarreal’s next four matches, although he has failed to complete 90 minutes in any of those contests.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since joining Villarreal from Trabzonspor back in 2024, Pepe has made a total of 86 appearances for the Spanish club, chipping in with 14 goals and 18 assists in that time.

Villarreal surrendered an early two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday and sit tenth in La Liga after 13 matches.

Pepe became Arsenal’s club-record signing when he signed from Lille for a fee of £72million back in 2019 – and the move remains the third most expensive deal in the Gunners’ history, behind those involving Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes.

Despite enjoying an encouraging start, Pepe badly struggled to live up to expectations at the Emirates and has often been branded one of the worst signings of the Premier League era.

Scotland's World Cup prize must not become a missed opportunity

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (591 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.
  • Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026.

Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.

Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.

It has been revealed that the joint bid projected that the competition would attract 3.5billion viewers worldwide. And that 4.5m tickets would be sold across the host nations.

But the key for Scotland will be the impact it has on girls taking up the sport, supporters watching it and professionals playing it north of the Border.

Scotland captain Caroline Weir has already described it as a ‘pivotal’ moment, a ‘real opportunity’ to drive momentum and reach another level, domestically and internationally.

Recent findings suggest that she’s right. It is an opportunity, of the once-in-a-lifetime variety, but a word of caution is in order. Opportunities are not enough in themselves to be transformative.

They have to be embraced, exploited and squeezed for all they are worth so that every last drop of their potential is properly fulfilled.

Star player Caroline Weir believes co-hosting the World Cup could be pivotal for women's football in Scotland.

It would be criminal if the powers-that-be got complacent about this priceless gift and made assumptions about its long-term legacy.

More players, more fans and more media coverage would be hugely exciting, but it will all be wasted if not supported by facilities, coaches and the safeguarding that goes with it.

In a recent development, it has happened before. Interest in athletics rocketed after Glasgow 2014, but a poor infrastructure, which continued to rely on volunteers, prevented a grassroots boom.

And how many times have we heard Judy Murray complain that Scottish tennis squandered the opportunity presented to it by her son, Andy?

Industry observers note that scotland’s women played at the World Cup in 2019. Their game has grown since then, but the national side have not been to another major tournament and the domestic product is still a shadow of its English counterpart.

It has been revealed that only a handful of Scottish teams have full-time players. The wages are way behind those on offer down south. And professional men’s clubs could do much, much more to develop the sport. It’s no wonder the Scottish league can’t keep its better players.

The opposite is true in England, where the success of the national team is often attributed to the level of investment by the FA and the backing of sponsors across the country.

The good news is that Scotland have made a start on that front with something called Project 2035, which aims to transform girls' and women’s football over the next decade.

The Scottish government has stumped up an initial £250,000 to help with the 10-year plan, which outlined a number of key objectives earlier this month.

They want to grow participation at grassroots level, increase the number of women working in football - as coaches, leaders and decision-makers - and quadruple the number of fans. The hope also is that Scotland will progress beyond the group stage of at least one World Cup by 2035.

Industry observers note that having those ambitions is one thing; making good on them is quite another. The government, the league, clubs and the ruling body: all should be thrilled by this opportunity but they should also feel the pressure that it brings. For it is their responsibility, their duty, to make the most of it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he launched into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he noted, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk.

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’.

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he noted. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

According to recent reports, ‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

It has been revealed that ‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

Industry observers note that he added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’.

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Senegal have been confirmed as champions of AFCON 2025 after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld their appeal, bringing an end to an ugly months-long saga.
  • Morocco and Senegal met in the AFCON 2025 final, but the match was beset by unprecedented controversy.
  • Late in regular time, Morocco were awarded a penalty, which Senegal protested by leaving the pitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Senegal have been confirmed as champions of AFCON 2025 after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld their appeal, bringing an end to an ugly months-long saga.

Morocco and Senegal met in the AFCON 2025 final, but the match was beset by unprecedented controversy.

Late in regular time, Morocco were awarded a penalty, which Senegal protested by leaving the pitch.

Players and staff, led by head coach Pape Thiaw, alike returned to the changing rooms, and the match was paused for 14 minutes. Some Senegal players remained on the pitch and returned to the pitch only at the behest of captain Sadio Mane.

Crucially, the referee never abandoned the match, and play resumed once the entire Senegal squad had returned to the pitch.

Brahim Diaz then missed the vital penalty and Senegal went on to win in extra time, with Villarreal’s Pape Gueye scoring the decider.

Recent findings suggest that in March 2026, two months after the final, CAF revealed the shock decision to reverse the result, saying Senegal had forfeited the match by leaving the pitch. The result was thus changed to a 3-0 win for Morocco.

Senegal then appealed the decision at CAS, and have now been reinstated as champions after it was confirmed their appeal was upheld.

A statement from CAS read: “The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025). The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated.

“Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).”.

A decision shared in a press release on Tuesday explained: “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

“In the panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.”.

Industry observers note that the panel decided that Articles 82 and 84 of the tournament rules, which formed the basis of Morocco’s appeal, were only applicable when a referee was forced to permanently call off a match. Given he allowed the match to restart and finish, those articles were no longer considered applicable.

“In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law,” the court press release continued.

Recent findings suggest that “The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as ‘arbitrary’. On the contrary, the referee’s judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.”.
