Should the game have been played differently?

In a recent development, “Frosinone played their game but made a few mistakes they don’t usually make, but that’s certainly not my concern, losing by such a large margin. What’s worrying are the mistakes we made that we could have avoided.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 07:16.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has warned Ethan Nwaneri that brief flashes of quality will not be enough to secure regular football at Borussia Dortmund.

The record-breaking 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga leaders on loan from the Gunners in the summer, but has struggled for opportunities in recent weeks.

Nwaneri could now face his parent club in Tuesday's Champions League meeting in north London, with Arteta making his expectations clear.

Nwaneri initially enjoyed opportunities in Niko Kovac's starting lineup after arriving in Germany, but his involvement has since diminished significantly.

The versatile attacking midfielder has not started a match in over a month and has played just five minutes across Dortmund's last three Bundesliga fixtures.

Arteta believes the teenager must show greater consistency to establish himself at the highest level, insisting that occasional impressive performances are not enough.

"We're talking here about the highest level in Europe," the Arsenal boss said (via the Evening Standard). "You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency.".

The Spaniard also stressed that Nwaneri must earn his place in a talented Dortmund squad, rather than expect opportunities because of his Arsenal background.

"He needs to earn the right to play," Arteta added, explaining that joining a major European club does not automatically guarantee minutes.

Arteta remains convinced that Nwaneri has the mentality and quality to succeed, but acknowledged that his loan spells at Marseille and Dortmund form part of a challenging development journey.

Arsenal are understood to have the option to recall the youngster in January if his situation does not improve, with Arteta at the moment unconvinced that the Dortmund move is delivering the desired benefits.

Nwaneri is eligible to feature against his parent club on Tuesday, although Dortmund's strong form makes a starting place appear unlikely.

Nevertheless, the opportunity to face Arsenal off the bench could provide the teenager with an ideal platform to respond to Arteta's comments, particularly after his recent lack of involvement.

The Gunners boss has challenged him to show consistency and earn his place, rather than rely on occasional moments of quality. A positive contribution against the Premier League champions would certainly help his case.

Should Nwaneri find the net, he could join a select group of players to score against their parent clubs while on loan, including James Rodriguez against Real Madrid and Philippe Coutinho against Barcelona during their respective spells at Bayern Munich.

It would be a significant way to make his mark, although simply earning meaningful minutes against Arsenal would represent an encouraging step in his Dortmund journey.

In a recent development, sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. In a recent development, “We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he remarked. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

According to recent reports, “Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Sources indicate that yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German remarked: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”.

In a recent development, in his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

You can also follow the latest updates from Manchester United’s crucial trip to Elland Road in our sister blog here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that latest catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement1, particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g. oxidative addition and reductive elimination). The widespread exploitation of systems based on main-group elements therefore requires alternative elementary steps to effect turnover. Herein, we demonstrate a new catalytic platform for nucleophilic fluorination, which exploits a complex based on calcium (the fifth most Earth-abundant element) as the fluoride delivery vehicle. The key intermediate is a calcium-fluoride complex featuring a terminal Ca–F interaction, a unique structural geometry enabled by a highly sterically encumbered dianionic ligand-scaffold. This intermediate links reactants and products through F– capture and release steps, and thereby unlocks catalytic F– shuttling. Late Ca–F bond breaking in the rate-determining fluoride-delivery transition-state means that electronic and steric tuning of F– by calcium is chemically significant; proof-of-concept results show a hitherto unprecedented level of selectivity for substitution over elimination brought about by Ca-modulation. In a broader context, this work demonstrates how control over catalyst speciation and reagent binding affinity are key factors for the future development of sustainable non-transition metal paradigms in catalysis.

Arsenal: 'Much more complete' - how Madueke has grown and become a key man amid injuries

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1307 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 07:45.
  • Noni Madueke's signing by Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had even stepped onto the pitch.
  • Arriving from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing and had to justify an investment in a player who initially seemed destined to be a back-up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 07:45.

Noni Madueke's signing by Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had even stepped onto the pitch.

Arriving from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing and had to justify an investment in a player who initially seemed destined to be a back-up.

Sources indicate that A little over a year later, the debate is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke has been given a longer run of opportunities and has taken the chance. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of this development.

Industry observers note that mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In a press conference, the manager highlighted the variety that the forward has added to the team's play and his contribution without the ball. And Madueke's growth has followed a concrete path.

Recent findings suggest that madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive the ball wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short burst of acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives the ball in equal-numbers situations.

Recent findings suggest that that characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In the 2024-25 season, he was one of the Premier League players who carried the ball into the box the most and created danger mainly through individual runs. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

It has been revealed that 'He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forward players. And he is doing it in several ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and a lot more connection to his game' - Arteta said.

It has been revealed that the numbers help to gauge the growth. According to FotMob's analysis for the 2026-27 Premier League, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, compared with 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although it is important to consider that Saka has played fewer minutes.

Industry observers note that the improvement also demonstrates in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

'And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball. So, I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying it a lot' - Arteta said.

The evolution, therefore, is not about abandoning the dribble but about knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, only now he seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

In a recent development, the comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical players. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right to cut inside, but they do so in different ways.

Industry observers note that saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and alternates between carries, short passes and crosses very naturally. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal's main attacking tools.

Madueke, for his part, offers more explosiveness in the first movement and tends to look for the individual duel more often. He is a more vertical player, who likes to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When he is confident, he can disorganise a defence without depending on a long build-up.

The creation data helps illustrate this difference. As well as outperforming Saka in chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob's analysis, Madueke also shows a greater volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps the advantage in shooting and defensive contribution indicators. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

Industry observers note that this difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka can be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that dismantles the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating situations of individual imbalance.

Industry observers note that the Englishman has also shown that he can play on the left, a role he performed when Christos Tzolis was unavailable. There, he needs to adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can look for the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta's options and prevents the team from depending on a single alternative for each side.

Sources indicate that the competition with Saka, therefore, does not need to be understood as an attempt to take the starter's place. Arsenal need more than one player capable of deciding matches, especially in a long season, with the Premier League, the Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is starting to offer arguments to be considered more than a simple replacement.

One detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

Sources indicate that arteta highlighted the player's reaction as an example for the rest of the squad. The manager mentioned that Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

Madueke at Arsenal, season by season.

Premier League 2025-26 vs. 2026-27, per-90 averages.

Recent findings suggest that premier League games only. Because the seasons have different numbers of minutes, the comparison uses per-90 averages; the total appears below each average. The change compares the averages. Madueke has not yet provided an assist in the Premier League in 2026-27. Data up to 21 November 2026 (matchweek 11).

Sources indicate that 'He went away, decided to train, came back, and he was a different Noni. You could sense that he meant business, and he was not going to accept that situation. Since then, he has been incredible' - Arteta explained, commenting on the player's change of attitude.

Recent findings suggest that the individual work, however, did not start now. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has been working for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention to the ability to be more decisive in the final third.

Recent findings suggest that the result has shown up in the numbers: his average of chances created has more than doubled compared with last season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate has risen from 50% to 55%, while his passing accuracy has gone from 78% to 87%. In open-play crosses, his success rate has jumped from 14% to 33%.

It has been revealed that these numbers help explain why Arteta talks about a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but he has started to execute better other actions that previously could limit his influence. The progress has come from different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 08:40, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 08:42.

James Tarkowski received his first-ever red card in the Premier League as Everton fell to a heavy 4-0 defeat at Brentford on Monday night.

The 34-year-old defender had previously been given 74 yellow cards across 350 Premier League appearances but had never been sent off – a top-flight record for the most yellows without ever seeing red.

However, Tarkowski was dismissed in the first half with the Toffees trailing by two goals at the Gtech Community Stadium for a studs-up challenge on the shin of Yehor Yarmolyuk.

Tarkowski had initially thundered into a sliding challenge and won the ball, but his right boot followed through with his studs scraping down the Brentford midfielder’s leg.

On-field referee Craig Pawson gave a yellow card for the challenge, but was then advised by VAR to review the incident at the pitchside monitor, where he ultimately came to the decision to upgrade the yellow to a red.

Tarkowski was deemed to have “committed a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety” with a red card issued for serious foul play.

Recent findings suggest that james Tarkowski is sent off! ? https://t.co/s5ta4f74np.

Tarkowski will therefore serve a three-match suspension and will crucially miss Sunday’s Merseyside derby against rivals Liverpool at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The Toffees captain is also banned for a trip to Aston Villa on December 2 and a home clash with Fulham four days later, but he is available to return for an away fixture against Brighton & Hove Albion on December 13.

After taking charge of his record-breaking 593rd game as Everton manager, David Moyes was asked whether the club will look to appeal the red card, and he told Sky Sports: "Don't know yet.

"I thought Tarki got the ball in plenty of time, certainly got there before the player who came in late, but I think Tarki's foot was high, and in that case then there is a chance it can be given.".

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Moyes added: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was, but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that.".

Sky Sports pundit and former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher believes that Tarkowski was right to be sent off and feels that Moyes has a “major problem” to deal with ahead of the Merseyside derby.

Sources indicate that "It is a red card. It might not have been a red card in 1996, but it is in 2026,” Carragher said on Monday Night Football.

"He knows what he's doing, and he doesn't need to do that. At the last moment, he is trying to pull back on the intensity of the challenge. Don't give [the referee] the option. He doesn't need to do that. I've made tackles like that.".

He added: "David Moyes should be looking at him and thinking [it's 2-0], you've left your mates out there with 10, and it's the Merseyside derby next.

"For me, it's the biggest game of the season. Everton, biggest game of the season. I hope for the Liverpool players and staff, the biggest game of the season.

It has been revealed that "He's brilliant in the box, and that will be a significant problem for Everton. He's so good set-piece-wise.".

Either Jake O'Brien or Michael Keane is expected to play at centre-back alongside Jarrad Branthwaite in the absence of Tarkowski in the next three Premier League games.

A four-goal defeat for Everton has seen them slip to ninth in the Premier League table, with Brentford leapfrogging them into seventh position, albeit sitting just one point above them.

Arsenal dropped two points in their 1-1 Champions League draw against Borussia Dortmund, so claims Noni Madueke.

The Gunners were dominant in the first half at Emirates Stadium, where Viktor Gyokeres' stunner put them into a 10th-minute lead.

Yet Arsenal could not add to their lead, and Dortmund stepped up in the second half, equalising in the 55th minute through Maximilian Beier.

Jobe Bellingham saw a goal disallowed, but Arsenal came on strong late on, with Gyokeres squandering a golden chance, while the Gunners hit the post twice.

Arsenal's 30 shots are their most on record in a Champions League game (since 2003-04), and the Gunners' most in a game that they failed to win across all competitions since December 2023 v West Ham.

And while Madueke felt some of Arsenal's play was "incredible", he acknowledged Mikel Arteta's team are frustrated.

He told Amazon Prime: "I feel like the performance from us up until the last shot was incredible at times.

Industry observers note that "Definitely feels like two points dropped. A bit of frustration; need to get all three points, I think.".

Gyokeres echoed Madueke's sentiment, though he is confident Arsenal will get better results if they keep on creating so many chances.

"We could have scored in the second half. We could have won the game in many different ways," he told Amazon Prime.

"We played well and created a lot of chances, we deserved to win the game but sometimes it is like that.

Sources indicate that "The most important thing is that we create those chances and get shots on goal. For sure we will score goals.".

Arsenal have failed to win a home game in the group stage of major European competition for the first time since November 2019 (2-1 defeat v Eintracht Frankfurt), ending a run of 18 successive victories – the longest such winning run by any side in major European competition history.

According to recent reports, arteta stated: "The performance was superb and there is no question about that from the start to the end. We played against a really good side and the domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more.

"I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.".

The Gunners are, though, only the third English side in Champions League history to go 20 successive matches unbeaten (W14 D6), after Manchester City between 2022 and 2024 (26) and Manchester United between 2007 and 2009 (25).

Now, their focus will turn to a huge Premier League clash with Man City on Sunday.

According to recent reports, "I think these are the best games. I'm really looking forward to it," Madueke added.

"Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same.

Recent findings suggest that "We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We're champions, we're at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates. There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction.".

Manchester United are furious at referees’ chief Howard Webb’s support for the decision to send off Leny Yoro at Liverpool, despite the defender having his one-match suspension removed.

The French centre-back was dismissed after only eight minutes of United’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday for fouling Reds striker Alexander Isak as he advanced towards goal, with referee Sam Barrott deciding Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United successfully appealed for wrongful dismissal and the suspension has now been removed, the Football Association has confirmed, meaning Yoro is free to play in the Premier League match against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Liverpool scored their opening goal directly from the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s challenge.

Sources indicate that one question raised was whether Isak had the ball sufficiently under control for this to count as denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. The Swede’s touch took the ball into the arms of United goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer Webb backed the decision to dismiss the 21-year-old, saying it was “certainly not clearly wrong”.

However, United boss Mauricio Pochettino vehemently disagreed and hit out at the lack of VAR intervention.

It is understood that the club are unhappy with Webb’s comments and strategy to make their feelings known to Pro Ref.

Speaking at a press conference ahead of his team’s Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, the Argentinian mentioned: “Very disappointed. My question always was the same, we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotion of the game, sometimes the view or the position can affect that. But if we have VAR, what were they doing?

“Now, are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play with similar tools – 11 v 11?

Sources indicate that “We have an unbelievable car, but we need to have the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way. We love the technology, yes, and we accept the technology is there, but what are they doing? But it’s not only this mistake, it affects everything.

In a recent development, “No-one is talking about the [Dominik Szoboszlai’s] goal wasn’t legal, they should have disallowed the goal because [Bradley] Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years the rules have changed while I was in America. Why didn’t they check it? It must be disallowed.”.

Webb discussed the sending-off with former Liverpool and United striker Michael Owen in the latest edition of Match Officials: Mic’d Up, which aired on Tuesday evening but was recorded before the FA confirmed Yoro’s suspension had been removed.

“The reason we’re talking about it is the fourth consideration [in DOGSO decisions], that’s control or likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball,” Webb noted.

Industry observers note that “Isak’s got control of the ball, he’s got possession, he’s got the touch, he knocks it past Yoro. He’s moving at pace at that moment and a crowd comes in and knocks him down.

It has been revealed that “There’s a question mark I guess around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

“The VAR checks to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn’t.

“I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving promptly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it’s a little bit debatable. (It’s) certainly not clearly wrong.”.

VAR John Brooks was of the same opinion as he said in the audio between him and referee Barrott: “Let’s roll it through firstly to see whether the attacker is going to get on the end of the ball.

Sources indicate that “Just roll through real speed. So, at full speed, Isak maintains his momentum and likely gets on the end of it.

According to recent reports, “OK, certainly not clearly wrong that he doesn’t. So I think the DOGSO confirmed.”.

Dundee manager Steven Pressley is nothing if not honest. Having taken full responsibility for his team’s 8-0 thrashing by Hearts on Saturday, he now admits that the experience left him wanting to ‘crawl under a rock and hide’.

Industry observers note that you won’t hear him writing it off as a ‘bad day at the office’ or branding it a freak result from which he and his players would quickly move on. Dundee’s heaviest-ever home defeat in the league was an indignity that really hit their popular manager. And hit him hard.

In a recent development, ‘It’s been a difficult 24-48 hours,’ said Pressley. ‘There’s been a lot of hurt, a lot of embarrassment. As you can imagine, at times I’ve wanted to crawl under a rock and hide.

‘It’s difficult on the back of such a disappointing result. But I will say this: I suffer a lot from vulnerability at times, but for some reason during difficult moments I seem to find strength from somewhere.

‘I don’t know if it’s from my family, from messages that I’ve received, from my reading. But I’ve had to show strength. I have to support the players. I have to make sure we navigate our way out of what was a really embarrassing moment.

‘We had a good meeting yesterday. We chatted a lot about the various aspects, and hopefully we can start responding to the disappointment.’.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley says he felt hurt and embarrassed after losing 8-0 to Hearts.

Defender Ryan Astley struggles to take in Dundee's heaviest-ever home defeat in the league.

That process starts tomorrow night against Hibs, who suffered a humiliation of their own when they lost 4-0 at home to Dundee United on Saturday. Pressley notes the immediate objective for his team is to go there with a better attitude than they have shown lately.

Recent findings suggest that he had feared a setback coming for Dundee – ‘not 8-0 but a disappointing performance’ – because he had ‘sensed a little bit of subconscious complacency’. He felt his team had been over-hyped by outsiders on the back of a start to the season in which they won five of their 12 matches before the international break.

According to recent reports, ‘We’re nowhere near the levels that people keep telling us we are,’ he said. ‘We’re not a good enough team not to do the hard yards. Our whole strength has been built on the cohesion of the team, the unity of the team, the aggressiveness of the team.

‘And I think what Saturday did highlight is exactly what I’ve been saying. If we get lazy on the hard yards, we’re a very vulnerable team. We have to be at our absolute best to get results.’.

He hopes the Hearts game will be ‘a reset moment’ that eventually helps his players to improve, but there are no guarantees from Pressley that they will shake it off at Easter Road tomorrow.

Asked if he expected a positive response from them, he said: ‘I don’t know. I know that they’re hurting. I know that they want to respond in the best possible way. That part I don’t question. I know how much it’s affected them.

‘But we’ve not had a lot of time. I just hope we can bring some pride back to the football club with the right type of performance.’.

According to recent reports, the good news for Dundee is that they are up against a team who have been hopeless in their own stadium recently. Second-bottom Hibs have lost nine of their last ten Premiership games at Easter Road and haven’t taken three points there since early April.

Supporters turned on the Edinburgh side after the defeat by Dundee United, but Hibs midfielder Jamie McGrath has dismissed the idea that he and his team-mates don’t enjoy playing in their own ground.

Jamie McGrath was in the Hibs side that suffered another defeat at Easter Road on Saturday.

In a recent development, ‘Personally, I always like playing at home,’ remarked McGrath. ‘I love the pitch, I love the stadium. It’s a significant open pitch, which I think should suit us. But for whatever reason, so far this season we haven’t been able to capitalise on playing at home.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s hard to put your finger on one certain thing. Maybe just being more decisive in both boxes or probably conceding goals at crucial times in the game, like after five minutes on Saturday, we just give ourselves a bit of a mountain to climb.’.

It looked like Marink Reedijk’s side had turned the corner when they followed up a rousing victory over city rivals Hearts in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final with a 4-0 win at Aberdeen in their last game before the international break.

So McGrath is hoping Saturday’s aberration was a blip. ‘We’ve been on a decent run the last month and probably the international break came at a tricky time for us. We were just kind of building momentum and had two good wins back-to-back against two good teams. It’s frustrating not to build on that.’.

McGrath is unfazed by Hibs’ lowly league position and senses a chance to change that with three matches in the space of nine days against other sides in the bottom six.

‘It’s not something that we’re concerned about at the minute. It’s obviously not where we want to be. We want to try to get closer to that top six and this two-week period is quite crucial. If you put a little run together, you can boost yourself right up the league.’.

It was rinse and repeat from an Arsenal perspective. Completely dominate the opening 45 minutes with some sublime football. Take the lead but then fail to kick on. Drop the intensity in the second half and regret those missed opportunities.

That happened against Slavia Prague, when the Gunners just about held on in the second half to win. It happened on Saturday, when they had to come from behind just to draw a match they should have been three or four goals up in.

Recent findings suggest that and it happened here, in perhaps the most ridiculous way yet. With some better decision-making in the final third, the Premier League champions might have put six past Dortmund.

According to recent reports, instead, from their 30 shots, Arsenal managed just four shots on target and one goal. The visitors rode their luck but they stayed within touch and when their moment came, Maximilian Beier took it with the kind of ruthlessness Arteta can only dream of.

It is unrealistic to expect the north Londoners to dominate a match for the full 90 minutes, even more so against Dortmund than the likes of Slavia Prague and Newcastle.

The problem is Arsenal’s lack of efficiency when they are on top means they cannot afford even the slightest drop in standards or intensity.

In a recent development, score the two or three goals that the dominance deserves in the first half and a dip after the break will not be so decisive. As it is, with Arsenal leaving the margins so thin, one moment is all it takes for the hard work to be undone.

At St James’ Park, that moment was Odegaard mis-kicking a clearance. Here, it was Joane Gadou charging away from Christos Tzolis and nobody in the home midfield coming across to cover.

Sources indicate that the match should have been done by then. Again, Arsenal were sensational in the first 45 minutes.

Noni Madueke, a constant threat, could not sort his feet out rapidly enough when a rebound fell to him. The winger was then completely open, screaming for the ball shortly after when Declan Rice instead went by himself and had his shot deflected wide.

Counters were wasted. Viktor Gyokeres, who opened the scoring with a superb strike from distance, suddenly could not hit the target. When Arsenal went in only 1-0 up, what followed next was as predictable as it was galling for the Gunners.

The level dropped just slightly and the Bundesliga leaders came back into the game, equalising ten minutes after the restart.

Even then, though, Arsenal should have been able to recover. Unlike against Slavia Prague or Newcastle, Arsenal did not fall away for an extended period. This match was there for them to win and the chances came thick and fast.

Gyokeres headed wide from a few yards out. The Arsenal fans spent almost the entire final half an hour screaming at the players to shoot as extra touches were taken around the area.

When Serhou Guirassy then bounced the ball off his body onto his own post not once but twice, Arteta collapsed to the ground in disbelief.

The winner would not come. A top-two finish, which was so important in last season’s run to the final, has now become much harder.

But that is what this side keep doing. They seem determined to make things hard for himself. Another match that should have been won inside an hour turned into a 90-minute slugfest.

With Arsenal hoping this is another long season domestically and in Europe, it is a habit they must shake fast.

#106953. Latest Update: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1170 w)

Latest Update: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1170 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

The plate and the photos are on show at the fresh exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, says exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

In a recent development, alongside Picasso, a surprising number of notable artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

Sources indicate that two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to issue a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

It has been revealed that still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

Recent findings suggest that however, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

It has been revealed that the dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked massive and dangerous.".

The endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian notes. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a newly introduced image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

The designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

Recent findings suggest that still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

But altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash." The exhibition includes halls that are open to small dogs and even features artworks and performances specifically designed for them.

The feedback Reckert's been getting in the run-up to the show also aligns with this cheerful image. She notes that hardly a day goes by without something arriving in the mail related to the dachshund — whether pictures, artworks or information about dachshund-related events.

"It's really crazy," she states, showing examples of the stuff she's received. "I've never had an exhibition that was greeted ahead of its opening in such a friendly, diverse way. It's almost a bit uncanny, really.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Original Article was published on 24 June 2026.

Retraction to: Nature https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10702-5 Published online 24 June 2026.

According to recent reports, the authors retract this article, following a suggestion from the editors. Shortly after publication, a preprint (subsequently published (see ref. 1 below)) by Till Sawala identified an inconsistency in our analysis. Our calculations were erroneously comparing the comoving distance between the observed galaxies to the luminosity distance between galaxies in the simulated mocks. Correcting these issues reduces the discrepancy between the observed and simulated samples to 1.48–2.75 sigma, depending on the sample construction. This falls below the standard significance threshold of 3 sigma in the cosmology literature.

Despite the revised uncertainties, our method remains valid and provides tentative evidence for anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of galaxies in the Universe. The revised paper, with corrected uncertainties, will be submitted to another journal. This retraction will contain a link to the new publication, if and when it is published.

Both authors agree with this retraction.

Jobe, the younger brother of Real Madrid star Jude, was unfortunate not to hit the winner as he followed in Julian Ryerson’s saved shot, which Kepa Arrizabalaga spilled.

Kevin De Bruyne has made his feelings for Manchester City crystal clear as he has spoken out for the first time since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations.

At the end of September, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

The Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts with a number of commercial partners to disguise secret funding of more than £830m and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

Man City continue to plead their innocence and lodged an appeal last month, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”.

A plethora of possible sanctions have been mooted should Man City’s guilty verdict be upheld, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

De Bruyne spent 10 glorious years at the Etihad Stadium before leaving in the summer of 2025 and will go down as one of Man City’s greatest-ever players after playing a crucial role in the club winning 19 trophies during his time at the club.

The Belgian playmaker won six Premier League titles, five EFL Cups and three FA Cups, while he also won the Champions League during a historic treble-winning season in 2022-23.

The two-time Premier League Player of the Season scored 108 goals and provided 177 assists in 422 appearances for Man City across all competitions, with 119 of those assists recorded in the Premier League to rank him second on the all-time list behind Ryan Giggs (162).

De Bruyne has made a welcome retuned to Manchester as his current club Napoli prepare to face City in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

While De Bruyne has acknowledged that some people may have different opinions over Man City’s guilty verdict, the legendary midfielder himself has insisted that his feelings towards the club will “never change”.

"My feeling's never been different,” he told reporters at a press conference. “Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group. Of course, it's a lot of things that's been going on but I cannot change anything about that.

In a recent development, "I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly... This is my club! I love the owners, I've talked about a lot of stuff outside of football, I've even spoken to Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] how to buy a club and everything, so there's a lot of things that goes around after this.

"I've nothing but affection for this club and that will never change! Even now, the people who treated me for 10 years exceptionally, my family and everything, that's for me the most notable and for me, that is it to be honest.".

Intense criticism has been aimed at Man City since the guilty verdict, but De Bruyne cannot "change anything" about people calling his former club a "disgrace" and still believes that everything he personally achieved with the club was won fairly.

In a recent development, “It [the verdict] still doesn’t change, my football has not changed,” De Bruyne said. “In life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit.

Recent findings suggest that “I played in between the white lines, I competed with other players and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That’s the thing I value most.

“In my career, the most key thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things.

Industry observers note that “I’ve given my all and that’s not going to change in my mind. I don’t think a lot of ­people will change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played. Other people may be disgraced a bit, but I can’t change anything about that.”.

Tuesday’s contest will mark De Bruyne’s second appearance back at the Etihad since departing Man City, and the 35-year-old will be hoping for a much smoother evening this time around.

On his previous visit last year, a first-half red card forced ex-Napoli boss Antonio Conte to reshuffle his side, with De Bruyne the unfortunate player to be sacrificed early in a 2-0 defeat.

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

According to recent reports, what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”.

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Industry observers note that was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

It has been revealed that the hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

Sources indicate that we have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

Having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Recent findings suggest that carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

According to recent reports, bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1.

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

United were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area demonstrated the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

According to recent reports, but after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

And that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick states he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

In a recent development, “But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

“There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”.

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick remarked he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”.

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”.

According to recent reports, martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick stated. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”.

It has been revealed that the Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

“It claims a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

“It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”.

It has been revealed that speaking to Sky Sports, he noted: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

According to recent reports, “We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

“They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

“It took us a little bit to adjust to it, but I don’t think it was too difficult to adjust. It was more down to us and maybe a lack of quality in the final third.”.

Middlesbrough have now won seven of their last nine league games against Swansea (D1 L1), as they moved one point clear at the top of the second tier.

Hellberg's side missed out on promotion to the Championship in 2025-26 after losing to Hull City in the play-off final, but the Middlesbrough boss was not getting too far ahead of himself, instead focusing on this Friday's clash with Southampton, their opponents amid the "Spygate" controversy last season.

"That makes it one year, 46 league games. It was a nice way to celebrate that," Hellberg said.

Industry observers note that "I think over 90 minutes we were quite good against a different challenge from the last game. It was more of an attacking game.

"I think we should have scored more goals, but we take 2-1 today and move on to Friday [against Southampton].

"Happy with the performance, happy with how much we created and happy with how few chances we gave away, even if they could have scored another one.

"I always felt we would create enough chances to win.".

  • Arsenal will be bidding to equal two all-time Champions League records when they welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium for Tuesday's league-phase encounter.
  • Mikel Arteta's men reunite with the German giants 12 years on from their last head-to-head in November 2014, when the Spaniard captained Arsenal to a 2-0 victory in North London.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 09:09.

Arsenal will be bidding to equal two all-time Champions League records when they welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium for Tuesday's league-phase encounter.

Mikel Arteta's men reunite with the German giants 12 years on from their last head-to-head in November 2014, when the Spaniard captained Arsenal to a 2-0 victory in North London.

The Gunners could end the evening top of the Champions League league phase table too, if they overcome Dortmund and Real Madrid - who are two points clear - either lose to PSV Eindhoven or draw and fall behind on goal difference; Paris Saint-Germain are not in action until Wednesday.

Arsenal have accrued 10 points from their opening four continental games this season, overcoming Lille, Slavia Prague and Napoli and only dropping points in an encapsulating 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

After also navigating the entire 2025-26 league phase unbeaten, Arsenal could firstly equal their own club record of 17 straight Champions League group stage/league phase games without suffering defeat.

Arteta's men have won 15 and drawn one of their 16 league-phase games since a 1-0 loss to Inter Milan in November 2024, and they have only ever gone 17 unbeaten at this stage between 2003 and 2006.

That record streak began with a 1-0 victory over Dynamo Kyiv in November 2003, and ended when Arsene Wenger's men suffered a 1-0 defeat to CSKA Moscow in 2006.

Additionally, Arsenal have won each of their last 12 Champions League group stage/league phase games at the Emirates and could equal the English football record for the longest victorious run on home soil.

The only Premier League team to win more successive UCL league phase/group stage games at home is Liverpool, who triumphed in 13 on the spin between 2020 and 2025.

Ever since their return to the Champions League in the 2023-24 season, Arsenal have been almost perfect at home in the group stage/league phase, and their 12-game winning run is a sight to behold.

Arteta's side kicked off their triumphant streak with a 4-0 rout of PSV Eindhoven in September 2023, before Sevilla and Lens were bested in the same year.

The 2024-25 group stage saw Paris Saint-Germain, Shakhtar Donetsk, Monaco and Dinamo Zagreb conquered in North London, while Olympiacos, Bayern Munich, Atletico Madrid and Kairat Almaty fell to Arsenal's Emirates might in 2025-26.

The Gunners' only home encounter in Europe so far this season ended in a 3-0 success over Lille, and they have scored a remarkable 36 goals while conceding just three during their 12-match sequence.

Thanks to Arsenal's prolonged absence from the Champions League between 2017 and 2023, it has been almost exactly 10 years since they last failed to win a group stage/league phase game at the Emirates; a 2-2 draw with Paris Saint-Germain on November 23, 2016.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri.

According to recent reports, I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Arsenal were fortunate not to concede a penalty against Borussia Dortmund during their Champions League draw.

The Premier League champions and Bundesliga leaders held each other to a 1-1 stalemate at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres’ rifled opener was cancelled out in the second half by Maximilian Beier.

It was the Gunners’ second draw on the spin after a 2-2 encounter at St James’ Park, where Noni Madueke rescued a point against Newcastle after Malick Thiaw and Harvey Barnes had put the Magpies ahead following Eberechi Eze’s opening goal.

But it was the goalscorer Gyokeres who almost turned from hero to villain, as he allegedly handled a Dortmund corner in the second period.

It led Amazon Prime Video pundits Alan Shearer and Mark Clattenberg to question referee Maurizio Mariani’s decision not to award a spot kick to the visitors.

“I think Arsenal were fortunate to have gotten away with that one,” Shearer stated on co-commentary.

"I know it might have been Fabio Silva in front of him trying to flick it on, but he didn't, and his arm is actually out.".

Clattenberg, noted alongside the record Premier League goalscorer in the north London gantry, concurred.

"We all know UEFA have a stricter handball rule than we see in the Premier League, but what doesn't save Gyokeres in this situation is, the ball comes in from a distance and he makes a little movement of his arm towards the ball so that makes it look more like a penalty kick for me,” the former official noted.

Former Arsenal forward Theo Walcott spoke of his relief at the penalty not being given.

"As soon as it hit his hand, straight away my heart is in my mouth, I think it's a penalty," he stated.

"I think he's got away with that. I'm pleased it wasn't given because it's not a penalty, but in Europe it probably should be.".

Gyokeres asserted his innocence in his post-match interview.

"I think the arm was towards my body," the Swede said.

"I don't think it was outside, so I don't think it was anything.".

Bruno Fernandes insisted his focus remained on turning Manchester United's fortunes around rather than putting pen to paper on a upcoming contract at Old Trafford.

Fernandes, who returns to Sporting CP with United in the Champions League on Wednesday, has been linked with a move away from the Red Devils over the last few years.

The 32-year-old was the subject of interest from the Saudi Pro League, while it has been reported he has turned down two offers to extend his stay with United.

Fernandes has a deal at Old Trafford until the end of the season, although the club hold an option to extend it through to June 2028, but the United captain's priorities lie on the pitch.

United were thumped 4-0 by rivals Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge, a result that leaves them 19th in the Premier League after 11 matches of the campaign.

Indeed, United's eight points this season are their fewest after 11 games of a league campaign since 1972-73 (seven). That is also the previous season in which the Red Devils only managed one win in their first 11 league matches.

"For us to start winning games, and then we can start speaking about a contract," Fernandes told reporters when asked about his future. "That's not important now, it's irrelevant.

"Obviously, I know it's my future, and I probably shouldn't look at it that way because I haven't got much left in my contract, but I'm not really worried about that.

"I'm more worried about getting results, trying to bring the club back into a position that we can be proud of, and we're not there at the moment.

"We're going to have time to speak about that. As I remarked, we had conversations.

"The conversations stopped at the moment that we thought that was not as important at the moment because results and performances were not at the level we should be.".

"There's still time for me to learn and become better." @B_Fernandes8 remains hungrier than ever to improve as a player and help the team https://t.co/PRwzDbI2G2.

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 24, 2026.

Fernandes joined United from Sporting in January 2020 and has become a crucial part of the Red Devils' midfield, but only has an FA Cup and EFL Cup to show for his efforts.

In fact, since moving to England, Fernandes has only played in one Champions League knockout tie, coming against Atletico Madrid back in 2022.

"As a player, you want to play the biggest tournaments, the biggest games," Fernandes added. "Sometimes it's not possible.

"When I started my career, I never had the opportunity in the first few years to play in the Champions League, so for me that was a dream far away, and I'm very proud of what I have achieved, even if I have only played one time [in the knockouts].

"I still have got time, I still have got many years left in my career, I hope so, and I'm going to have many opportunities to do that, and why not this season?".

With his penalty against Roma last time out, Fernandes netted his 24th goal in major European competition for United, moving ahead of Cristiano Ronaldo into seventh spot on the club's all-time scoring list, and he will be hoping to have another impact at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

Sources indicate that however, United are winless in their last six Champions League away games (D2 L4), losing both this season. They last had a longer winless run away from home in the competition between February 2004 and December 2005 (eight matches – D3 L5).

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 09:31.

Struggling on the pitch, Manchester United are already preparing for the January transfer window with three positions targeted and seven options identified.

Recent findings suggest that 19th in the Premier League, Manchester United are going through a sporting crisis. Mauricio Pochettino has just arrived to replace Michael Carrick. The Argentinian boss will try to halt the negative spiral, while the hierarchy is already preparing its next January transfer window.

The Manchester club intend to use January to strengthen their squad. According to TeamTalk, the club's decision-makers have identified three priority positions: centre-back, left-back and centre-forward. Signing a centre-back is Manchester United's main priority.

The club already have three profiles in mind: Calvin Bassey (Fulham), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton) and Nathan Collins (Brentford).

The club's executives have reportedly already made enquiries about all three players. A permanent transfer would, however, be needed to convince any of these clubs, with a loan not being considered in these cases.

Recent findings suggest that A large part of the winter budget should therefore be devoted to this signing. Manchester United's January budget is reportedly £50m, according to the Daily Mail. That is a rather small amount to strengthen in three positions and cover for the shortcomings of a squad in the midst of doubt.

In attack, Manchester United want to sign a centre-forward capable of providing more competition. Two options stand out: Folarin Balogun (Monaco) and Ivan Toney (Al-Ahli). A loan with an option to buy is reportedly being considered for both forwards, while Joshua Zirkzee could leave in January.

The club want to provide an additional solution on the left flank, where Luke Shaw lacks competition and availability.

In a recent development, two players are particularly liked: Alejandro Balde (Barcelona) and Rayan Ait-Nouri (Manchester City). Talks have reportedly already taken place with both clubs.

It has been revealed that both full-backs could leave in January as they play little at their respective clubs. Manchester United would favour a loan for one of these deals. The club have therefore already drawn up their roadmap, but the sporting situation and the meagre budget will not make it easy for them to strengthen.

These gaps in weather data affect forecasts everywhere: plugging them is not charity

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (990 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Observations from data-scarce regions, such as low-lying island Tuvalu in the South Pacific, are crucial to weather forecasts, early warning systems and climate-information services elsewhere.
  • It has been revealed that when I talk about collecting essential weather and climate data in countries with limited resources, many take it to mean that wealthier countries, institutions and firms should ‘help poorer ones’.
  • Industry observers note that that’s the resounding conclusion of a report published this month by The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) in collaboration with the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Observations from data-scarce regions, such as low-lying island Tuvalu in the South Pacific, are crucial to weather forecasts, early warning systems and climate-information services elsewhere. Credit: Mario Tama/Getty.

It has been revealed that when I talk about collecting essential weather and climate data in countries with limited resources, many take it to mean that wealthier countries, institutions and firms should ‘help poorer ones’. But as a development and climate-finance executive, I know that this is an investment rather than an act of charity. Science proves it: better forecasts at home rely on observations abroad.

Industry observers note that that’s the resounding conclusion of a report published this month by The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) in collaboration with the World Meteorological Organization (WMO). The report was commissioned by the Systematic Observations Financing Facility (SOFF), a United Nations fund dedicated to basic weather and climate data around the world, of which I am a director.

It has been revealed that its aim was to establish the benefits of filling gaps in the WMO’s Global Basic Observing Network (GBON), which defines member nations’ mandatory weather-station coverage. To comply, each country must have a land station every 200 kilometres, as well as a weather balloon every 500 kilometres over land and every 1,000 kilometres over sea to collect data on essential variables (such as temperature, pressure, humidity and wind).

Global climate body fights for survival: why the IPCC must be saved.

Global climate body fights for survival: why the IPCC must be saved.

It has been revealed that but agreeing on standards and sites is not the same as having the economic means to implement them. Since 2023, GBON stations have been required to share their data. Yet, about 90% of weather data from low-income countries and small island nations are not being shared. Some data are not even collected because many stations are missing, stopped working or cannot transmit their measurements.

It has been revealed that these gaps don’t just impede local forecasts, they affect regional and global projections too. Daily weather data feed into increasingly sophisticated computer models that predict how weather systems around the world evolve.

Think of a weather forecast as a photograph. It is made up of millions of pixels, each contributing a small piece of information. Weather forecasting is more complex, but the analogy helps to explain the problem: if too many ‘pixels’ are missing, the global picture is blurry or incomplete. And for forecasts, some ‘pixels’, or observations, are more valuable than others. Plugging gaps in data-scarce regions is the best way to improve forecasts everywhere.

Industry observers note that it is also a matter of justice: on average, a seven-day temperature forecast in a high-income country is as accurate as a one-day forecast in a low-income country (M. Linsenmeier and J. G. Shrader Nature Commun. 17, 10792; 2026).

The results of the ECMWF simulations are striking. Better coverage in low-income countries and small island states can cut uncertainty in 12-hour local forecasts by more than 30% in parts of Africa and by up to 20% across the Pacific.

Extra data in all countries eligible for development assistance and small island nations would improve the accuracy of temperature and wind forecasts up to six or seven days ahead in the tropics, home to some 40% of the world’s population, and in the Northern Hemisphere’s mid-latitudes, where much of Europe, North America and northern Asia sit. This would help with, for example, aviation and maritime operations, planning of agricultural activities, water management and preparations for severe weather.

Disparity in countries’ capacity to finance weather observations is striking. To quantify the inequality, SOFF developed an indicator comparing countries’ gross dom-estic product (GDP) with the geographical area for which they are mandated to provide observations, including marine exclusive economic zones. For example, although it is a small country, Switzerland has a larger budget than does Tuvalu, a Pacific island nation spread across an immense ocean area (Switzerland’s GDP is around 300,000 times larger per square kilometre). Yet both countries contribute to and benefit from the same global observing system.
